outcomes: A workspace keeps its work items in one Jira Cloud project and its skills speak only the tasks contract
A Jira workflow's own statuses map to the contract's states by status category, so no status name is configured
A retry after a lost answer finds the ticket the first attempt created instead of creating it again, and an outcome the provider cannot establish is reported as unresolved
A Jira credential is sent only to the bound site and appears in no answer, message or log
nonGoals: The proposals, memory and missions contracts: Jira holds no change proposals
Assignment, hierarchy and exclusive claims: tasks assign, link and claim are not offered
Jira Data Center and Server: only Jira Cloud's REST API v2 is spoken
Rich text: a description is the plain string REST API v2 serves, never Atlassian Document Format
Detecting a concurrent writer between the read and the write of a checked precondition, or two concurrent creates with one idempotency key
Running the live proof in the ordinary gate: it mutates a real Jira project and runs only on request

requirements.text: A task's state is read from its status category: To Do is open, In Progress is in_progress, Done is done, and Done with the resolution Won't Do or Duplicate is canceled; providerState is the status name. A transition takes the first transition Jira offers into the target category, sets the resolution Won't Do for canceled, and leaves a task already in the state as it is. blocked has no category: a transition or create to it is unsupported, and find matches nothing for it.

A revision is v and the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the JSON array of summary, description, status name, status category, resolution, sorted labels and sorted assignee account ids, so it changes whenever anything a task shows changes, a done task becoming canceled included.

find reads the bound project with JQL built from the request's text, states and labels, oldest key first. The caller's text and labels are quoted and cannot add a clause. Pages cover every issue present throughout a traversal exactly once, whatever page sizes the caller asks for.

create records the idempotency key as a hidden label and the request's digest as an issue property, in the create call itself. A repeated key returns the ticket it created, even before Jira's search shows it, and the key with other content is a conflict. Every write is sent once; after a lost answer or a 5xx the provider reads Jira back and answers from what it finds, never with a second ticket, and an outcome it cannot establish is unresolved, never retryable, and names what settles it. The idempotency label never appears in a task's labels and a request carrying one is refused.

Failures keep their meaning: a missing issue or a reference another source issued is not found, an outage is unavailable and writes nothing, a rate limit is retryable and never repeated, a refused credential is denied, and a stale expectedRevision is a conflict that names the current revision.

The provider reads JIRA_EMAIL and JIRA_API_TOKEN itself, sends them only to the bound site over https or to a loopback stand-in, and removes the token, its Basic form and every string shaped like an Atlassian API token from everything it writes, Jira error messages included.

The manifest passes the extension protocol's strict validation, declares preconditions checked where Jira cannot compare and write in one step, and marks every operation as reaching outside the machine.
